sentences.text: The Integrated Tactical Management Position is the primary workstation for real-time coordination of Meridian departure flow, arrival flow, airport capacity, and airspace constraints.
It presents a combined tactical view so that the Regional Flow Manager can compare planned demand, measured throughput, and active control measures without changing applications.
The Common Situation Display provides the base map, timeline, flight list, and measure status panels used at the position.
The Regional Flow Platform synchronizes the tactical display with the Time Synchronization Service so that all timestamps, countdowns, and validity intervals use the same operational clock.
The Arrival Regulation Console is also known as Nightjar at the Integrated Tactical Management Position, where the alias is displayed only in operator profile help text.
Arrival demand is monitored against the Airport Acceptance Rate, current sequencing performance, and any Ground Delay Program that remains in effect.
The Tower Supervisor uses the display to see runway assignment pressure, airborne sequence spacing, and expected crossing points at the North Runway Meter and the South Runway Meter.
Emberline sends revised departure metering advisories when runway demand exceeds the configured queue threshold.
Skylark must refresh the apron movement layer within five seconds of each validated surface event.
The Slot Allocation Engine produces the Pushback Window Token when the agreed departure window is frozen for tactical execution.
The Airport CDM Portal exposes agreed Target Off Block Time values and stakeholder remarks to the tactical position in read-only mode unless the operator has an assigned coordination role.
The Demand Prediction Service continuously updates short-term traffic forecasts using the Flight Intent Message stream and recent airport performance history.
The Capacity Assessment Module recalculates available capacity when runway configuration, weather category, staffing assumptions, or sector workload changes.
The Airspace Sector Planner monitors sector demand through the Sector Load Monitor and confirms whether proposed measures are compatible with en route capacity.
The Military Airspace Liaison can mark an airspace release or closure assumption for review before it affects tactical flow calculations.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies weather impacts shown from the Weather Ingest Gateway before the position applies weather-driven capacity values.

The Airport Duty Manager can declare Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, or Contingency Fallback State from the tactical header after coordination is complete.
When the operating state changes, the Business Rules Registry supplies the applicable thresholds for alerting, approval routing, and measure publication.
The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative review proposed timing changes in the same timeline used by flow staff, which reduces duplicate verbal coordination.
The Ground Handling Dispatcher uses the Handling Resource Planner view to compare planned off-block demand with available servicing capacity at affected stands.
The Gate Conflict Detector highlights stand conflicts that would undermine a proposed departure recovery plan or compress arrival unloading capacity.
A Tactical Regulation Proposal can be drafted directly from the display, checked against current capacity assumptions, and routed through the Alert Distribution Hub for stakeholder acknowledgement.
Accepted adjustments are reflected as Calculated Takeoff Time updates, Slot Compliance State changes, or airport capacity annotations depending on the measure type.

Every operator action, system recommendation, acknowledgement, and rejected alternative is written to the Collaborative Decision Log and the Audit Event Ledger for traceability and post-operation analysis.
